extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audiobooks were downloaded using LibriLight tools, and text sources were extracted using custom parsers or manual approaches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox and text from Project Gutenberg and other domains.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio data was downsampled, segmented into 10-20 second chunks, and text was normalized by removing unwanted characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels were generated via beam-search decoding, matched to source text using TF-IDF and Smith-Waterman alignment, and development/test sets were human-verified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training of ASR systems, multilingual ASR, and Text-to-Speech (TTS) research.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset, a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research.

description.evidence: This paper introduces Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset, a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages

url.evidence: The dataset will be made freely available for anyone at http://www.openslr.org .

license.evidence: LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data are released in the public domain, which allows us to release MLS freely to everyone.

creator.evidence: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert

publisher.evidence: Facebook AI Research, Menlo Park & Paris, USA & France

inLanguage.evidence: Based on the number of audiobook hours and the availability of the corresponding text sources of the audiobooks, we have selected English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish for the MLS dataset preparation.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: For downloading the LibriVox audiobooks in these languages, we have used data preparation tools available at LibriLight open source library... We have written parsers to automatically extract the text for each of these domains and downloaded the text sources for all the audiobooks in English.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We have written parsers to automatically extract the text for each of these domains and downloaded the text sources for all the audiobooks in English.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages... most of which being based on the Project Gutenberg text data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: All the audio data is downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz for further processing... we segment the audio files into 10-20 second segments... we first perform NFKC normalization and remove all the unwanted characters like punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols etc.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We generate pseudo labels for the segmented audio samples by performing a beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model... We retrieve the documents which best matches with the pseudo label for the audio segments using term-frequency inverse document-frequency (TF-IDF) similarity score on bigrams. We then perform a Smith-Waterman alignment... The human transcribers listen to the audio file while looking the transcript and are asked to correct the transcripts if they find any mistakes.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we have used wav2letter@anywhere framework to perform the inference in a streaming fashion.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Second, we label the gender of all the speakers with a gender classifier.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We believe this dataset will promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and in multilingual ASR. This dataset can also be used for Text-to-Speech (TTS) research by extending the LibriTTS [25] dataset
